A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPELL research despite the changed title and layout. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation benchmarks, diversity comparisons, shielding experiments, and ablations, including Tables 1–2 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds empirical results on runtime, prompt length, two-moons sampling, and watermark occurrence.

M1.justification: The sparse ReLU correction, predicted-output shielding, static and dynamic reference sets, overcompensation, and nearest-neighbor implementation are retained. Algorithms 1–2 describe the same procedure. Inter-batch repellency was already present in v1.

E1.justification: ImageNet-1k and CC12M remain the principal evaluation datasets. v3 adds supporting coverage through unconditional two-moons generation in Figure 3 and qualitative generation from MS COCO prompts outside Simple Diffusion's training data in Appendix N. Prompt-length stratification reuses existing CC12M coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated diversity-method comparators remain Particle Guidance, CADS, and Interval Guidance, alongside unmodified diffusion controls. The new runtime comparison reuses this comparator set. Newly discussed anti-memorization and negative-guidance methods are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds several distinct evaluation procedures: timing 500 images with batch size 8 on a V100, stratifying CC12M prompts into ten length groups, and counting watermarks in 1,600 images per condition for Simple Diffusion and 800 for Latent Diffusion. The two-moons demonstration uses 200 samples and radius 0.075. These are added protocols; the existing main benchmark settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix K tests whether diversity gains persist for longer, more specific prompts. Appendix N adds watermark error analysis and qualitative cases, while Appendix G investigates computational overhead. These substantially expand the diagnostic questions examined. The earlier radius, guidance-weight, and intervention-dynamics analyses are retained, including the radius plot moved to Appendix M.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains mean and standard deviation over five independent seeds. New reporting includes standard errors over five seeds for the prompt-length analysis and chi-square tests with Yates' correction for watermark frequencies. No increase in the main benchmark's run count is reported.

E6.justification: Table 1's numerical results and Table 2's shielding rates are retained. New results include runtime measurements, prompt-stratified findings, and additional metric combinations in Table 4. Appendix N reports 62/1600 versus 105/1600 watermarked Simple Diffusion outputs without versus with SPELL, with p=0.001; the corresponding Latent Diffusion counts are 79/800 versus 98/800, with p=0.15. These are newly reported findings, not version-to-version performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendices A–C retain the Doob/DPS derivation, disjoint-shield guarantee, and conservative-field argument. Theorem 1 becomes Theorem C.1 without a substantive mathematical change. The new sampler qualification appears in the discussion rather than a revised proof or formal assumption.

C1.justification: The central diversity, shielding, and scalability claims remain. v3 removes the introduction's claim that using expected final outputs distinguishes SPELL from Particle Guidance, emphasizing sparsity instead. The discussion also drops v1's advertised machine-unlearning application in favor of shielded generation.

C2.justification: v3 adds a substantive qualification about forward-process expectations and probability-flow ODE sampling. It explains cancellation between overlapping shields more explicitly and develops a hypothesis that watermarks facilitate movement between modes. It also expands interpretation of dataset-dependent coverage and attributes large-reference-set overhead specifically to CPU nearest-neighbor search.

D1.justification: Table 4 newly discloses comparator tuning values, including PG strengths, IG intervals, and CADS parameters. v3 also specifies runtime hardware and batch settings, CPU neighbor search, and 1024x1024 resolution for the retained SD3 example. The original implementation pseudocode and core hyperparameters remain unchanged; these disclosures do not establish changes to existing experiments.

R1.justification: The new Related Works section substantially expands positioning around anti-memorization, negative guidance, and sequential Monte Carlo, including Chen, Koulischer, Kim, Liu, and Thornton. It acknowledges that Particle Guidance can also operate on expected final outputs, shifting the principal distinction to sparsity and fixed reference sets. The earlier unlearning framing and associated citations are removed.

P1.justification: The title, contribution bullets, results discussion, and several headings are revised. Related work becomes a separate section, appendix organization changes, and the misleading 'throughout training' ablation heading is corrected to generation. Much of the background, method exposition, and original appendix prose remains intact.

P2.justification: The main paper changes from a single-column layout to a two-column conference format, with substantial figure and table rearrangement. v3 adds the two-moons and prompt-length plots, Tables 4–5, and ten qualitative image panels. Figure 4 gains a fourth tradeoff plot; v1 Figure 3 moves to v3 Figure 26, and Figure 6 trims the existing 16-image sequence to 14.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through disclosed baseline settings, runtime measurements, prompt-length checks, and investigation of increased watermark occurrence. Its expanded related-work discussion and sampler qualification make novelty and applicability easier to assess. Reporting the unfavorable watermark finding strengthens the paper's treatment of tradeoffs, although its proposed mechanism remains speculative. The core method, proofs, and main benchmark evidence remain largely unchanged, making the overall gain incremental.
